statement: This file plans how the data of the stateful units the draft moves is carried to STACKIT, for the families of data stores that have a planner (families). It moves no data and opens no connection: every step is for a person. A number in it is the customer's own statement (origin CUSTOMER_INPUT, with the answer it came from) or it is UNKNOWN; a quantity nobody stated is never zero. A duration is a lower bound of the transfer alone and a comparison with the accepted downtime says only whether that bound exceeds it, never that the window fits. Stateful units of other families have no plan here.

rto.reason: the plan states what the method is designed to give and does not compute with the stated objective: a person compares the two, and the rehearsal measures the time

assets.rollback: Before the connection strings are switched nothing is switched: the source was neither stopped nor made read-only nor changed after the freeze, so it is current to the freeze; stop the writers, put the recorded connection settings of the source back and start the writers on it. After the switch, what was written to the target is not on the source: the point of no return is the first write to the target. The way back is a copy in the other direction (the same method, a separate rehearsal) or accepting the loss; take that decision before the window. There is no reverse replication defined on STACKIT. Keep the target until the cause is known and do not delete the source in the same hour.

the extension list is the one STACKIT documented when read (2026-10-18); an instance is the authority (`SHOW extwlist.extensions;`)

assets.rollback: Before the consumers are switched nothing is switched: the source bucket was neither changed nor made read-only after the freeze, so it is current to the freeze; stop the writers, put the recorded endpoint, bucket name and credentials of the source back and start the writers on it. After the switch, what was written to the target is not in the source: the point of no return is the first write to the target through the switch (a new object, an overwritten one or a delete, and the versions the target creates if versioning is on). The way back is a copy in the other direction (the same tool with the two ends swapped, a separate rehearsal; the retention and the version history of the source cannot be recreated by it) or accepting the loss; take that decision before the window. This plan defines no reverse replication. Keep the source until the cause is known and do not delete it in the same hour.
limits: StackToIT moves no data and opens no connection: every step is defined for a person to run; none is applied or verified by this plan
the commands are templates for rclone with a Cloud Storage remote; no copy was run against a STACKIT bucket by this build, and the documentation read for them is cited with each check
the Terraform shows neither the size of the data (the customer's input source.dataset.size) nor the number of objects (no input states it; the preflight counts them)

what a copy does not carry is the checks versions, object-lock-retention, encryption, acl-and-policy, object-metadata, requester-pays and soft-deleted-objects; the settings of the bucket itself are the NOT CARRIED lines of storage.tf and the decision records, and this plan does not repeat them

not verified on STACKIT: the throughput, a multipart upload of every object (--s3-upload-cutoff 0) at large sizes, the behaviour of per-version writes and delete markers, and the limits of the endpoint
not read for this plan: the Google pages on requester pays, uniform bucket-level access and the soft delete policy; the commands that name them are templates to check against the gcloud reference
Google bills the network egress of the data read out of the bucket and the retrieval fee of the colder classes; the plan computes no cost
a duration is a lower bound of the transfer alone and the window of the final pass has no formula: it depends on what changed since the last pass
